subject: scorching desert heat
title: The 5 Hottest Temperatures Ever Recorded, Ranked (#1 Has Stood Since 1913)

scenes.text: The five hottest temperatures ever recorded, ranked. Number one was measured before World War One.

scenes.label: Turbat · 53.7 °C
scenes.text: Number five: Turbat, Pakistan, May 2017. 53.7 Celsius, nearly 129 Fahrenheit. The World Meteorological Organization took two years to verify it.

scenes.label: Mitribah · 53.9 °C
scenes.text: Number four: Mitribah, Kuwait, July 2016. 53.9 Celsius, 129 Fahrenheit. The official record for all of Asia.

scenes.label: Tirat Tsvi · 54 °C
scenes.text: Number three: Tirat Tsvi, Israel, June 1942. 54 Celsius, about 129 Fahrenheit, in the Jordan Valley, and it took 74 years for anywhere in Asia to come close.

scenes.label: Kebili · 55 °C
scenes.text: Number two: Kebili, Tunisia, July 1931. 55 Celsius, 131 Fahrenheit, the hottest reading ever taken in Africa.

scenes.label: Furnace Creek · 56.7 °C
scenes.text: Number one: Furnace Creek, Death Valley, California, July 10, 1913. 56.7 Celsius, 134 Fahrenheit, at a place that was then called Greenland Ranch.

description:
The five highest air temperatures officially recognised by the World Meteorological Organization, ranked.
Turbat, Pakistan reached 53.7 °C on 28 May 2017 and Mitribah, Kuwait 53.9 °C on 21 July 2016, both verified by the WMO in 2019 as the third and fourth hottest readings ever and the record for Asia. Tirat Tsvi, Israel recorded 54.0 °C on 21 June 1942, Kebili, Tunisia 55.0 °C on 7 July 1931, the African record, and Furnace Creek in Death Valley, California 56.7 °C (134 °F) on 10 July 1913, the world record.
Which of these could you survive an afternoon in?
first_comment: Some weather historians doubt the 1913 Death Valley reading and would hand the record to Kebili or to newer Death Valley readings, but the WMO still lists 56.7 °C as official. Which would you have put at number one? And what should we rank next: the wettest places on Earth?
